doctrine: Single source of physics defaults for the Wright Flyer program. Every value carries per-value sources, a dossier record link, a convention label, and a status: verified (primary/authoritative agreement), verified-range (range is solid, point value is not), tunable-with-provenance (sources disagree or boundary undocumented — simulation exposes it as a config with the variants listed), absent-by-verification (verified to NOT exist in primary sources; any number used is inference and labeled so). Silent keeping of unverifiable values is forbidden.

wingspan_m.convention: tip-to-tip full span b (geometry-conventions-v1: b is ALWAYS full span)

sources: wright-brothers.org Flyer_I (single source; NASM/NPS publish no gap)
wing_gap_m.convention: vertical separation between plane chords; whether leading-edge or quarter-chord datum is UNSTATED by the source

anhedral_droop_m.convention: total tip droop relative to center section

sources: Orville (1902, after restoring droop): 'the trouble experienced heretofore with a crosswind turning up the first wing it struck had been overcome' — NASM 'Researching the Wright Way' + Wright-diary-derived accounts
anhedral_intent.convention: PROMOTION over the plan's Round-2 demotion: a direct Wright-era source exists, so lesson copy MAY state gust-response intent with this citation

sources: AIAA 2004-0211 (span 12 ft, chord 2.5 ft per surface)
AIAA 2004-0211 citing Culick (single source); 1905 increased to 11.7 ft
canard_arm_m.convention: WING-to-canard distance, NOT CG-to-canard; CG arm must be derived from the mass build-up, never assumed equal

sources: AIAA 2004-0211 verbatim: canard deflection limits 'have not been reported in the literature nor in the blueprints of the Smithsonian'; ±30° obtained by 3D-model matching against the first-flight photograph; beyond 30° adds no control power. ±15° is documented only for the 1905 Flyer.
canard_travel_deg.convention: VERIFIED ABSENT from primary sources; simulation exposes travel as a tunable with the photo-inference provenance; E1.5 owns any refinement

sources: AIAA 2004-0211 + wrightflyerproject.org + legacy.wrightflyer.org: 20 ft² (avg span 6.9 ft, chord 1.5 ft) — engineering lineage
rudder_area_m2.convention: projected area, both movable surfaces; 20 ft² default (stronger engineering pedigree), 21 exposed as variant; NASM publishes none

variants.note: live variant, convention difference unresolved (E1.9 projected-vs-developed candidate)

gross_weight_kg.convention: gross = empty + pilot; pilot mass itself single-source, exposed as tunable in H-cases

engine_displacement_m3.original: 201 in³ (4.0 in bore × 4.0 in stroke, 4 cyl)

engine_power_w.original: 12 hp sustained at ~1025 rpm; ~16 hp cold at start, dropping as it heats
engine_power_w.convention: sustained shaft power; the cold-start transient is a SEPARATE modeled effect (E4 propulsion), never averaged in

variants.note: thermal transient, load-bearing for the launch phase

sources: wright-brothers.org: 180 lb (magneto/flywheel/water inclusion unstated; 20-lb flywheel drives the magneto)
engine_mass_kg.convention: NO source defines the mass boundary; the E1.9 six-bucket convention (dry/installed/cooling/ignition/drivetrain/propellers) must be populated by E1.5/E1.6 dossier work; until then the mass build-up uses 180 lb 'installed-ambiguous' with these variants exposed

chain_ratio.original: 23:8 (8T crank, 23T propshaft), one chain crossed for counter-rotation
sources: wright-brothers.org spec PDF; arithmetic-consistent: 1025 rpm × 8/23 ≈ 357 ≈ reported ~350 prop rpm
chain_ratio.convention: reduction crank→prop; crossed chain in guide tube

sources: Smithsonian propeller record A19830381000 (8½ ft; two laminations 1¾-in spruce, linen tips, aluminum-varnish)
prop_diameter_m.convention: diameter; wright-brothers.org's '8 ft' is a rounding outlier

prop_rpm_flight.original: ~350 in flight; design point 330 rpm at 24 mph
prop_rpm_flight.convention: operating range 330-357; exact per-flight rpm unknowable

prop_efficiency.original: modern measured >75% at first-flight conditions, peak ~82%
sources: Smithsonian: 66% is WILBUR'S OWN CALCULATED figure, not a measurement
prop_efficiency.convention: convention with every number (plan law): 66% = Wilbur-calculated; 75-82% = modern tunnel-measured on reproductions; simulation targets come from a2-props-bentend curves, never the 66% folklore

airspeed_dec17_mps.original: ~31 mph through air (telegram); NPS 30-34 mph range
sources: LOC telegram: 'average speed through air thirty-one miles'
NPS teaching materials: 6.8 mph ground into 27 mph wind ≈ 34 mph air
airspeed_dec17_mps.convention: AIRSPEED; ground speed ~7-10 mph; range honest because the wind measurement itself varies

static_pitch_stability.original: statically unstable; barely stabilizable by trained pilot
static_pitch_stability.convention: open-loop longitudinal; quantitative poles are V-02a gate territory

sources: NPS Four Powered Flights (canonical 120 ft/12 s)
Orville's DIARY (day-of): 'out about 100 feet from the end of the tracks... Time about 12 seconds (not known exactly as watch was not promptly stopped)'
120 ft figure lineage: Orville's 1913 Flying article
flight1_distance_m.convention: H-case anchors use DISTRIBUTIONS: diary says ~100 ft from track end, canonical 120 ft is later-account; both lineages recorded per WindReference doctrine

variants.note: primary; datum ambiguity (track end vs liftoff point)

sources: Orville diary: 'Dist. not measured but about 175 ft'
DIARY gives NO distance or time for flight 3 ('out about the same distance as Will's', height 'probably 12 to 14 feet'); 200 ft/15 s comes from Orville's 1913 later account
flight3_distance_m.convention: weakest-sourced flight; H-case weighting must reflect that

sources: Orville diary: 'The distance over the ground was 852 feet in 59 seconds' — the ONLY precisely measured flight; telegram's '57 seconds' is a transmission error
flight4_distance_m.convention: ground distance; landing broke the canard frame; the machine-destroying gust rollover was a SEPARATE later event (John T. Daniels caught inside)

wind_dec17_mps.original: diary: 'a little over 20 miles (corrected) 27 miles according to the Government anemometer'; telegram: 21 mph; later account: 24-27 mph over the flights
wind_dec17_mps.convention: WindReference disaggregation (E1.8): Wrights' hand-held Richard anemometer ~20+ mph vs government Weather Bureau 27 mph; heights unrecorded; the simulation treats wind as a distribution spanning instruments, never one number

launch_rail_length_m.original: 60 ft monorail (four 15-ft 2x4s), metal-capped edge, bicycle-hub dolly; liftoff after ~40 ft run on Dec 17
launch_rail_length_m.convention: level ground per telegram ('started from level')

derrick_height_m.original: 20-ft tower / 16-ft weight drop (technical literature) vs 30-ft derrick (NPS/National-Register lineage)
sources: wright-brothers.org catapult reconstruction: ~20-ft salvaged windmill tower, seven 200-lb weights (max 1400 lb), 16-ft drop, 3:1 pulley SPEED multiplication (1 ft drop → ~3 ft pull, ~466 lb continuous pull, ~50 ft of pull)
NPS CLI/1971 National Register lineage: 1600 lb from a 30-ft derrick
derrick_height_m.convention: PLAN CORRECTION: the plan's '30 ft (not 16)' flag mixed quantities — 16 ft is the DROP DISTANCE in the 20-ft-tower lineage, not a competing tower height; both lineages live; pulleys multiply DISTANCE not force; first catapult use 1904-09-07

huffman_prairie.original: cow pasture (Torrence Huffman, rent-free); first circle 1904-09-20 (Wilbur, ~4080 ft in 1:16); witness Amos I. Root (Gleanings in Bee Culture, 1905-01-01)

flight_1905_oct5.original: 24 1/5 mi in 39 min 23.8 s, ~29-30 circuits, ended by fuel exhaustion
sources: Wrights' own record (primary preset per plan §3.3 choice)
variant: Bishop Milton Wright's diary '24 miles in 38:04'
flight_1905_oct5.convention: PRIMARY = Wrights' record; distance is circuit-length × laps (computed ground track), stays inside the 2x2 km tile (E1.3 validates)

big_kill_devil_hill_m.original: ~90 ft today (stabilized); ~100 ft bare shifting dune in 1900-03
big_kill_devil_hill_m.convention: powered flights from the LEVEL PLAIN north of the hill, not the dune; camp = 1901 shed (lengthened, living quarters ~42x16 ft) + 1903 hangar (~44-48x16 ft, NPS internal variants)

sand_roughness_z0_m.original: 1e-3 to 1e-2 m band; bare smooth patches near 1e-4 to 1e-3
sources: Davenport-Wieringa classification (AMS Glossary; featureless sand 0.0002-0.005 m, short grass 0.008-0.03 m)
Levin et al. 2008 coastal-dune z0 measurements
sand_roughness_z0_m.convention: no Kitty-Hawk-specific measurement exists; z0 is a distribution axis in E1.8/E3.3, never a point claim

glides_1902.original: the Wrights' own estimate, Sept 19 - Oct 24 1902; no complete log kept
glides_1902.convention: 'almost 1000' is the top of the estimate range; any single number is unsupported (narrative use only)

no_claims: Reference values, not model claims. Evidence colors for simulation outputs are assigned by the V-case program; a 'verified' status here means the HISTORICAL value is well-sourced, not that any model reproduces it.
